summary.oneLiner: SETL completed its transformation into an integrated turnkey solutions provider with FY26 revenue up 26.7% to INR 793cr, though Q4 margins dipped to 15.5% due to commodity inflation and preemptive hiring. The INR 1,000cr order book and upcoming INR 130cr capex (targeting INR 4,000cr total capacity) position the company for accelerated FY27 growth, leveraging new Japanese tech partnerships and subsidiary synergies.
summary.business: The Company designs, engineers, manufactures, installs, commissions and provides lifecycle support for process equipment used by regulated process industries, having evolved from a glass lining equipment manufacturer into a multidisciplinary engineering platform. Its capabilities span glass-lined equipment, process systems, bioprocess solutions, heat transfer equipment, filtration, drying, vacuum technologies and engineering services, delivered to customers across domestic and international markets. In its BRSR the Company reports a single business activity - manufacturing of glass-lined equipment and stainless steel and high alloy equipment, including reactors, receivers, storage tanks, filters, vacuum pumps and allied process equipment, with turnkey solutions primarily for the pharmaceutical and chemical industries - accounting for 100% of turnover.

Vacuum and pumping systems (S2 Stanpumps: Customised pumping systems for vacuum distillation, solvent recovery and specialised fluid handling
Bioprocess and life sciences (Standard S: Equipment design, process engineering, facility integration and lifecycle support
Chillers: Chillers market entered through an agreement with Climaveneta Climate Technologies Private Limited

Engineers Private Limited, M/s Higenic Flora Polymers and M/s Yashasve Glass Lining, plus the acquisitions of Standard C2C Engineering Private Limited and Scigenics (India) Private Limited; the material subsidiary acquired the metal business from M/s S2 Engineering Services and the pumps business from M/s Stampumps Engineering Industries|International partnerships and shareholder backing: investment from AGI Group (Japan), an agreement with Climaveneta Climate Technologies Private Limited, a Supply and Purchase agreement with Gale Process Solutions LLP (USA), a long-term agreement with M/s. Biocon Solutions Pte Ltd (Singapore) and a 3-year performance agreement with API Pharma (UAE)|Reference installed base in regulated industries dating to the supply of its first unique stainless-steel glass-lined reactor to NATCO Pharma Limited|Disciplined capital structure - management states it maintained a disciplined capital structure in FY26 supported by a strong balance sheet that provides flexibility to pursue strategic growth opportunities|Human capital depth: the Group employed 859 full-time employees plus 125 trainees and interns as at March 31, 2026, with average employee experience of 6.62 years and a stable attrition rate of 10%
currentContext.strategies: Build an integrated engineering platform rather than operate as a manufacturer of individual equipment - bringing process engineering, detailed design, precision manufacturing, automation, installation, commissioning and lifecycle support under one organisation so customers engage a single engineering partner across the project lifecycle|Expand the addressable market beyond traditional glass-lined equipment into turnkey engineering projects across pharmaceuticals, chemicals, biotechnology, food processing and other allied process industries, improving the quality of the revenue mix|Grow through selective acquisitions and technology collaborations that add complementary capability rather than scale alone - during FY26 the integration of Scigenics and Standard C2C Engineering broadened engineering expertise and strengthened the bioprocess and life-sciences presence|Run two complementary growth engines: the core process-industry engineering business, and entry into the AI infrastructure ecosystem through a planned investment in GScale Energy covering power and cooling infrastructure for AI data centres|Drive manufacturing and operational excellence - invest in manufacturing flexibility, throughput, quality systems, automation, digital manufacturing and engineering standardisation across facilities|Deepen the global technology partnership with GL Hakko Co., Ltd. of Japan in glass-lined process equipment|Expand the global footprint by strengthening overseas subsidiaries, technology collaborations and regional partnerships to improve market access and diversify the revenue base|Invest in engineering talent, product development, manufacturing capabilities and technologies to participate in the next generation of industrial growth
currentContext.expansion: FY26 is described as a defining step in the evolution of the Company's manufacturing capability - a shift from specialised equipment production toward a comprehensive, vertically integrated engineering ecosystem. The expansion came mainly through integration rather than a disclosed greenfield project: the integration of Standard Scigenics extended precision manufacturing into bioprocess, high-purity, biopharmaceutical and life-sciences applications, while the integration of Standard C2C Engineering brought multidisciplinary design and turnkey execution capability (civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation scopes) into the platform. These sit alongside sustained investment in manufacturing infrastructure, automation and digital engineering technologies - multi-axis CNC machining centres, automated and robot-assisted welding systems, collaborative robots, coordinate measuring machines, non-destructive testing, real-time production monitoring and data-driven quality control - and a deepened global technology partnership with GL Hakko Co., Ltd. of Japan in glass-lined process equipment. Footprint as stated in the Manufacturing Excellence section: 9+ manufacturing facilities, 180+ engineered product lines and 7 lakhs Sq Ft+ of manufacturing and engineering space; BRSR Section A separately reports 5 plants and 1 office in India and no international plants or offices, and the MD&A notes that all manufacturing facilities are located in Telangana, with expansion into additional geographies being evaluated to reduce location concentration risk. The Company journey timeline records the completion of a new glass lining equipment facility at the SGL Unit and the commencement of operations at Unit 5. Forward expansion is directed at AI data centre infrastructure through power and cooling solutions. No rupee capex quantum, no commissioning dates and no capacity-addition figures are disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
currentContext.mdna: Growing demand from process industries - expansion in pharmaceutical, specialty chemical and food & beverage industries is expected to drive demand for high-quality, corrosion-resistant and regulatory-compliant process equipment|Import substitution and Make in India - focus on domestic manufacturing and government support for localisation create opportunities for Indian manufacturers to replace imported process equipment|Technology upgradation and digitalisation - adoption of automation, IoT-enabled systems and predictive maintenance offers scope for differentiated, higher-margin products|Export growth potential - rising demand for cost-effective, quality-assured engineering equipment across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa|China +1 manufacturing strategy - supply-chain diversification away from China positions India as an alternative sourcing destination for engineered process equipment|Benefits from PLI schemes - government Production Linked Incentive schemes for pharmaceuticals and chemicals are expected to support capacity expansion and equipment demand|Threat: macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty - slowdowns, inflation, geopolitical tension and policy instability may adversely impact capital expenditure cycles across key customer industries|Threat: raw material price volatility - fluctuations in steel and alloy prices may impact input costs and operating margins|Margin lever/headwind: employee benefit expenses and other operating costs tied to capability expansion; FY26 employee benefit expenses were 5.61% of revenue from operations

risks.risk: Geographic concentration - all manufacturing facilities are located in Telangana
risks.note: Flagged in the MD&A as Concentration Risk: regional disruptions such as political instability, natural disasters, regulatory actions or workforce-related challenges could adversely affect operations and logistics. Mitigation is disaster recovery and business continuity measures, regular risk assessments, and expansion into additional geographies being evaluated.

risks.risk: Raw material dependency and price volatility (stainless steel, nickel alloys, castings)
risks.note: MD&A Dependency Risk: supply disruptions or price fluctuations may affect operations and profitability; the BRSR separately lists Responsible Supply Chain & Material Sourcing as a risk, noting dependence on critical raw materials and specialised suppliers exposes the Company to supply disruption, price volatility and quality risk. Mitigation is long-term supply arrangements, buffer inventory for critical materials, alternative sourcing, a diversified supplier base and a Supplier Code of Conduct.

risks.risk: Customer capital-expenditure cycle exposure to macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions
risks.note: Listed among Threats in the MD&A: economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures, geopolitical tensions and policy instability may adversely impact capital expenditure cycles across key customer industries - the Company sells capital equipment, so demand tracks customer capex.

MD&A Compliance Risk: operations are subject to environmental, labour and manufacturing regulations, and non-compliance or delays in obtaining statutory approvals could result in penalties, reputational risk or operational disruption. Mitigated through dedicated compliance teams, regular audits, certifications and timely infrastructure upgrades.

risks.risk: Product quality, warranty and liability risk in critical process applications
risks.note: MD&A Obligation Risk: product defects or non-conformance to industry specifications could lead to warranty claims, reputational damage, customer dissatisfaction and legal liabilities. Mitigated through stringent quality control across manufacturing units, relevant ISO certifications, warranty provisions in financial planning and customer feedback mechanisms. Product Quality & Customer Satisfaction is also the first material issue in the BRSR, treated there as an opportunity.

risks.risk: Working capital intensity and interest-rate exposure
risks.note: MD&A Exposure Risk: working capital requirements and interest rate fluctuations may affect liquidity, finance costs and profitability. Mitigated through diversified banking relationships and continuous monitoring of receivables, inventory cycles and working capital.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety in manufacturing operations
risks.note: The only material issue the BRSR classes as a risk with negative financial implications arising directly from operations: heavy equipment, fabrication processes and hazardous materials expose employees to occupational health and safety risk. Mitigated through an occupational health and safety management system, regular safety training and inspections, PPE and emergency preparedness and incident reporting.

risks.risk: Business ethics and corporate governance risk
risks.note: BRSR material issue: failure to maintain high standards of governance and ethical conduct may result in regulatory action, reputational damage and loss of stakeholder confidence. Mitigated through governance policies, a Code of Conduct, a whistle-blower mechanism and periodic compliance reviews under Board oversight.

one-line thesis: SETL completed its transformation into an integrated turnkey solutions provider with FY26 revenue up 26.7% to INR 793cr, though Q4 margins dipped to 15.5% due to commodity inflation and preemptive hiring. The INR 1,000cr order book and upcoming INR 130cr capex (targeting INR 4,000cr total capacity) position the company for accelerated FY27 growth, leveraging new Japanese tech partnerships and subsidiary synergies.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 793cr (+26.7% YoY); Q4: INR 231cr (+35% YoY). EBITDA: INR 138cr (+15.2% YoY), Margin 17.4% (Q4: 15.5%, down from ~17-19% prior quarters due to metal price hikes and manpower investment). PAT: INR 83cr (+21% YoY), Margin 10.5%. Order Book: >INR 1,000cr (approx. INR 30cr exports, rest domestic). Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but working capital days improved to 150 from 174; Operating Cash Flow positive at INR 45cr. One-offs: Q4 margin pressure from raw material costs and strategic hiring for future scale.
guidance: Revenue Growth: FY27 expected to be 'better' than FY26 (>26.7%), with quarterly run-rate targeting INR 250-300cr. Margins: Expected to improve in FY27 (>17.4%) driven by operating leverage and solution-mix. Order Inflow: Healthy pipeline, export revenue doubled in FY26, expected to grow further. Capex: INR 130cr over 2 years (INR 65cr in FY27) for Greenfield; INR 35-40cr for brownfield modernization.
order book & pipeline: Total >INR 1,000cr; Execution timeline 8-10 months. Exports constitute ~INR 30cr currently. Subsidiary C2C holds INR 46-47cr. Mix skewed domestic (>95%).
segment / subsidiary detail: Glass-Lined: Core profit driver, ~30% of revenue mix but transitioning. New Products: Shell & Tube Glass-Lined Heat Exchangers (200 units in OB, 100 delivered, local mfg starts July 2026 @ 200 units/month capacity). Bioprocess: Scigenics contributing ~INR 20cr in FY26, targeting INR 60cr in FY27. Engineering: C2C contributed INR 24cr in FY26, targeting INR 60cr in FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: Greenfield 36-acre campus (Phase 1 Apr 2027, Phase 2 Apr 2028) adds INR 2,000cr capacity; Brownfield modernization adds another INR 2,000cr; Total target capacity INR 4,000cr. Entry into Nuclear, Oil & Gas, Food & Beverage sectors. Pre-cast building capability to accelerate turnkey project timelines to 6-12 months.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 Gross Margin declined to 32% (from 39% in Q3) due to metal price volatility and upfront hiring. Management guides margin recovery in FY27 via operating leverage, higher value-add 'solution' selling vs pure equipment, and procurement discipline.
capex / expansion: FY26: INR 40cr. FY27 Plan: INR 65cr (Greenfield) + INR 35-40cr (Brownfield automation/robotics). Total 2-year outlay INR 130cr for Greenfield.
capital allocation: Focused on capacity expansion (Greenfield/Brownfield) and inorganic growth (integration of Scigenics/C2C). No dividend/buyback commentary; reinvestment mode for scale.
risks & watch-items: Raw material (metal) price volatility impacting short-term margins. Execution risk on large turnkey projects. High inventory levels (INR 438cr, though <180 days aging) tying up working capital. Geopolitical delays in export shipments.
management quality / tone: Highly confident, emphasizing 'best year in history', structural transformation complete, and long-term ambition. Aggressive on capacity and global expansion (Japan+India model).
non-obvious takeaways: Shift to 'pre-cast' civil construction to avoid traditional EPC delays and maintain high-speed project delivery (6 months for blocks). Explicit entry into Nuclear sector confirmed. Japanese ED appointment signals deepening of tech-transfer and global sales channel beyond just sourcing.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraint and need for specialized glass-lined/nuclear-grade equipment | Specialty Chemical & CDMO Players | beneficiary | High | SETL's expanded capacity and turnkey capability directly address the capex boom in Indian pharma/chemicals, offering import substitution for complex heat exchangers. |
| Rising input costs and margin pressure | Pure-play Equipment Fabricators | loser | Med | Competitors lacking integrated engineering/subsidiary synergies may struggle to match SETL's solution-based pricing power and margin resilience in FY27. |

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs, engineers, manufactures, installs, commissions and provides lifecycle support for process equipment used by regulated process industries, having evolved from a glass lining equipment manufacturer into a multidisciplinary engineering platform. Its capabilities span glass-lined equipment, process systems, bioprocess solutions, heat transfer equipment, filtration, drying, vacuum technologies and engineering services, delivered to customers across domestic and international markets. In its BRSR the Company reports a single business activity - manufacturing of glass-lined equipment and stainless steel and high alloy equipment, including reactors, receivers, storage tanks, filters, vacuum pumps and allied process equipment, with turnkey solutions primarily for the pharmaceutical and chemical industries - accounting for 100% of turnover.

- Mr. Kandula Ramakrishna — related party: Key Managerial Personnel - Director.
- Venkata Mohana Rao Katragadda — related party: Executive Director, DIN 08362181; signs Form AOC-1 for and on behalf of the Board alongside the Managing Director.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Glass-Lined: Core profit driver, ~30% of revenue mix but transitioning. New Products: Shell & Tube Glass-Lined Heat Exchangers (200 units in OB, 100 delivered, local mfg starts July 2026 @ 200 units/month capacity). Bioprocess: Scigenics contributing ~INR 20cr in FY26, targeting INR 60cr in FY27. Engineering: C2C contributed INR 24cr in FY26, targeting INR 60cr in FY27.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Glass-lined equipment:** Glass-lined reactors, Stainless-steel glass-lined reactor, Glass Lined Shell and Tube Heat Exchangers
- **Stainless steel and exotic alloy process equipment (S2 Engineering Industry):** Reactors, Pressure vessels, Filters, Dryers, Storage tanks, Heat exchangers, Thermal control systems
- **Vacuum and pumping systems (S2 Stanpumps):** Industrial vacuum pumps, Customised pumping systems for vacuum distillation, solvent recovery and specialised fluid handling
- **PTFE-lined process equipment and flow control (Standard Flora):** Lined pipes, Fittings, Valves, Expansion joints, Instrumentation, Customised components
- **Bioprocess and life sciences (Standard Scigenics):** Injectable manufacturing facilities, Bioprocess systems, Equipment design, process engineering, facility integration and lifecycle support
- **Process equipment and turnkey engineering (CPK Engineers):** Reactors, Filtration and drying systems, Storage tanks, Heat exchangers
- **Engineering and project management services (Standard C2C):** Engineering design, Procurement support, Construction supervision, Project controls, Cost estimation
- **AI data centre infrastructure:** Power and cooling solutions
- **Chillers:** Chillers market entered through an agreement with Climaveneta Climate Technologies Private Limited

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body: - ISO certifications - the Company states it maintains relevant ISO certifications across all manufacturing units; the individual standards are not named in the report

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Total >INR 1,000cr; Execution timeline 8-10 months. Exports constitute ~INR 30cr currently. Subsidiary C2C holds INR 46-47cr. Mix skewed domestic (>95%).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: FY27 expected to be 'better' than FY26 (>26.7%), with quarterly run-rate targeting INR 250-300cr. Margins: Expected to improve in FY27 (>17.4%) driven by operating leverage and solution-mix. Order Inflow: Healthy pipeline, export revenue doubled in FY26, expected to grow further. Capex: INR 130cr over 2 years (INR 65cr in FY27) for Greenfield; INR 35-40cr for brownfield modernization.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Greenfield 36-acre campus (Phase 1 Apr 2027, Phase 2 Apr 2028) adds INR 2,000cr capacity; Brownfield modernization adds another INR 2,000cr; Total target capacity INR 4,000cr. Entry into Nuclear, Oil & Gas, Food & Beverage sectors. Pre-cast building capability to accelerate turnkey project timelines to 6-12 months.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Growing demand from process industries - expansion in pharmaceutical, specialty chemical and food & beverage industries is expected to drive demand for high-quality, corrosion-resistant and regulatory-compliant process equipment
- Import substitution and Make in India - focus on domestic manufacturing and government support for localisation create opportunities for Indian manufacturers to replace imported process equipment
- Technology upgradation and digitalisation - adoption of automation, IoT-enabled systems and predictive maintenance offers scope for differentiated, higher-margin products
- Export growth potential - rising demand for cost-effective, quality-assured engineering equipment across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa
- China +1 manufacturing strategy - supply-chain diversification away from China positions India as an alternative sourcing destination for engineered process equipment
- Benefits from PLI schemes - government Production Linked Incentive schemes for pharmaceuticals and chemicals are expected to support capacity expansion and equipment demand
- Threat: macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty - slowdowns, inflation, geopolitical tension and policy instability may adversely impact capital expenditure cycles across key customer industries
- Threat: raw material price volatility - fluctuations in steel and alloy prices may impact input costs and operating margins
- Margin lever/headwind: employee benefit expenses and other operating costs tied to capability expansion; FY26 employee benefit expenses were 5.61% of revenue from operations

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 Gross Margin declined to 32% (from 39% in Q3) due to metal price volatility and upfront hiring. Management guides margin recovery in FY27 via operating leverage, higher value-add 'solution' selling vs pure equipment, and procurement discipline.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focused on capacity expansion (Greenfield/Brownfield) and inorganic growth (integration of Scigenics/C2C). No dividend/buyback commentary; reinvestment mode for scale.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 is described as a defining step in the evolution of the Company's manufacturing capability - a shift from specialised equipment production toward a comprehensive, vertically integrated engineering ecosystem. The expansion came mainly through integration rather than a disclosed greenfield project: the integration of Standard Scigenics extended precision manufacturing into bioprocess, high-purity, biopharmaceutical and life-sciences applications, while the integration of Standard C2C Engineering brought multidisciplinary design and turnkey execution capability (civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation scopes) into the platform. These sit alongside sustained investment in manufacturing infrastructure, automation and digital engineering technologies - multi-axis CNC machining centres, automated and robot-assisted welding systems, collaborative robots, coordinate measuring machines, non-destructive testing, real-time production monitoring and data-driven quality control - and a deepened global technology partnership with GL Hakko Co., Ltd. of Japan in glass-lined process equipment. Footprint as stated in the Manufacturing Excellence section: 9+ manufacturing facilities, 180+ engineered product lines and 7 lakhs Sq Ft+ of manufacturing and engineering space; BRSR Section A separately reports 5 plants and 1 office in India and no international plants or offices, and the MD&A notes that all manufacturing facilities are located in Telangana, with expansion into additional geographies being evaluated to reduce location concentration risk. The Company journey timeline records the completion of a new glass lining equipment facility at the SGL Unit and the commencement of operations at Unit 5. Forward expansion is directed at AI data centre infrastructure through power and cooling solutions. No rupee capex quantum, no commissioning dates and no capacity-addition figures are disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, emphasizing 'best year in history', structural transformation complete, and long-term ambition. Aggressive on capacity and global expansion (Japan+India model).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Single-partner, concept-to-commissioning model: end-to-end capability across design, engineering, manufacturing, installation, commissioning and lifecycle support enables customers to execute complex projects through one trusted partner
- Portfolio breadth - more than 180 products and turnkey engineering solutions spanning glass-lined equipment, process systems, bioprocess solutions, heat transfer equipment, filtration, drying, vacuum technologies and engineering services
- Capability built through acquisition: the businesses of C.P.K. Engineers Private Limited, M/s Higenic Flora Polymers and M/s Yashasve Glass Lining, plus the acquisitions of Standard C2C Engineering Private Limited and Scigenics (India) Private Limited; the material subsidiary acquired the metal business from M/s S2 Engineering Services and the pumps business from M/s Stampumps Engineering Industries
- International partnerships and shareholder backing: investment from AGI Group (Japan), an agreement with Climaveneta Climate Technologies Private Limited, a Supply and Purchase agreement with Gale Process Solutions LLP (USA), a long-term agreement with M/s. Biocon Solutions Pte Ltd (Singapore) and a 3-year performance agreement with API Pharma (UAE)
- Reference installed base in regulated industries dating to the supply of its first unique stainless-steel glass-lined reactor to NATCO Pharma Limited
- Disciplined capital structure - management states it maintained a disciplined capital structure in FY26 supported by a strong balance sheet that provides flexibility to pursue strategic growth opportunities
- Human capital depth: the Group employed 859 full-time employees plus 125 trainees and interns as at March 31, 2026, with average employee experience of 6.62 years and a stable attrition rate of 10%

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material (metal) price volatility impacting short-term margins. Execution risk on large turnkey projects. High inventory levels (INR 438cr, though <180 days aging) tying up working capital. Geopolitical delays in export shipments.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Shift to 'pre-cast' civil construction to avoid traditional EPC delays and maintain high-speed project delivery (6 months for blocks). Explicit entry into Nuclear sector confirmed. Japanese ED appointment signals deepening of tech-transfer and global sales channel beyond just sourcing.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraint and need for specialized glass-lined/nuclear-grade equipment | Specialty Chemical & CDMO Players | beneficiary | High | SETL's expanded capacity and turnkey capability directly address the capex boom in Indian pharma/chemicals, offering import substitution for complex heat exchangers. |
| Rising input costs and margin pressure | Pure-play Equipment Fabricators | loser | Med | Competitors lacking integrated engineering/subsidiary synergies may struggle to match SETL's solution-based pricing power and margin resilience in FY27. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Rename] Now Standard Engineering Technology Limited, 'Formerly known as Standard Glass Lining Technology Limited', with the 2026 milestone slide recording 'New Name and Change in Object'.
- [Acquisition - GScale] The deck gives two readings of the same transaction: slide 5 and the deal dashboard state a '51% strategic stake' / '51% Equity Stake - Controlling acquisition of GScale Energy', while the business-highlights slide says 'The Company has proposed to acquire controlling stake of 51% in M/s. GScale Energy Private Limited subject to regulatory approvals.(33.55% successfully acquired)'.
- [Acquisition - GL Hakko] 'Completed Phase I of its strategic investment in GL HAKKO Co., Ltd., Japan, acquiring a 19.19% stake. Phase II will increase the stake to up to 51.07% over the next three years, subject to regulatory approvals.' A 'Revenue target of Rs. 400 Cr' is attached to the Scale step of that roadmap, though the deck does not say whose revenue it refers to.
- [Leadership] GScale is led by founder and MD Kasu Brahma Reddy, cited as 25+ years in critical infrastructure, 486 MW delivered and 1 GW+ under execution across Tier-IV facilities, and 'Up to 765/400 kV industry-first power & grid connectivity frameworks'; he is now shown on SETL's leadership team.
- [Governance and ESOP] NRC approved a grant of 6,00,000 ESOPs under the ESOP 2024 Scheme (Grant I); Mr. Yasuyuki Ikeda proposed for redesignation from Non-Executive to Executive Director and Mr. Kancherla Uma Maheswara Rao proposed as Independent Director, both subject to shareholder approval; a subsidiary 'Standard Projects Private Limited' was incorporated.
- [API Pharma UAE] Slide 5 lists 'API Pharma UAE Wholly owned subsidiary' while the 2026 milestone entry describes a '3-year performance agreement with API Pharma (UAE) covering pharma, biopharma, life sciences, F&B & process industries' - the deck does not reconcile the two.
